significance: The royal temple of the Bangli kingdom, standing in terraces up a hillside with an eleven-tiered meru and a padmasana for Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva; copper-plate inscriptions from the 9th to 13th centuries mention it, and royal officials once swore their oaths of office here.
story: Villagers read the sacred banyan in the outer courtyard as an omen: a branch falling to the north-east foretells a king's death, one to the north-west a brahmin's.
